MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Centre

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for genetic susceptibility to BRCA-related cancer

CLINICAL INDICATION
Assessment of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome susceptibility

TEST PERFORMED
BRCA1 and BRCA2 Full Gene Analysis
- Comprehensive sequencing of all coding exons and intron-exon boundaries
- Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA) for large deletion/duplication analysis

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from peripheral blood lymphocytes. Analysis included:

1. Sequencing Analysis:
   - Unidirectional DNA sequencing with bidirectional confirmation of variants
   - Complete coverage of coding regions plus flanking splice sites (±20bp)
   - Fluorescent dye-terminator Sanger sequencing methodology
   - Detection sensitivity: >99% for point mutations

2. Dosage Analysis:
   - MLPA using GeneDose kits M42-C1 (BRCA1) and M67-B2 (BRCA2)
   - Detection of large deletions and duplications

Combined analytical sensitivity: >98% for BRCA1/BRCA2 mutations

RESULTS

BRCA1 (GenBank U14680.1): No pathogenic mutations detected
- Full gene sequencing: Normal
- MLPA analysis: Normal copy number

BRCA2 (GenBank U43746.1): No pathogenic mutations detected
- Two heterozygous variants of unknown significance identified:
  1. c.2883G>A (p.Gln961Gln) - Synonymous variant
  2. c.8331+18C>T - Intronic variant
- MLPA analysis: Normal copy number

VARIANT ANALYSIS
Pathogenicity assessment performed using GeneAnalyst v2.5 software suite:
- Protein prediction tools: ProteinEffect, SequenceAlign
- Database interrogation: dbSNP, ClinVar, BRCA Exchange
- Splicing algorithms: SplicePrediction, ExonScan

Both variants classified as Variants of Unknown Significance (VUS)

SUMMARY
No pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations were identified. Two variants of unknown clinical significance were detected in BRCA2. The clinical significance of these variants cannot be determined at this time based on current evidence.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Presymptomatic testing for the identified variants is not recommended for family members
2. Consider testing affected family members to help investigate the significance of these unclassified variants
3. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss results and implications
4. Variant reclassification may occur as additional evidence becomes available

TECHNICAL NOTES
This test detects point mutations and small insertions/deletions in coding regions and splice sites, as well as large deletions/duplications. Mutations in regulatory regions, deep intronic mutations, and some complex rearrangements may not be detected. Variant interpretation is based on current scientific knowledge and may change over time.
